title: Rom 8:30 golden chain: calling precedes justification
source_text: XVI. Praecipue vero hic valde observandus est Pauli locus, qui habetur Rom. 8. v. 29. 30. Ubi Apostolus seriem & catenam contexens gratiarum & beneficiorum, quae ex aeterno Dei in electos amore manant, & singula suo ordine recensens, vocationem diserte praeponit justificationi, tanquam aliquid quod eam antecedit. Nam, inquit, quos praescivit, etiam praedestinavit conformes fieri imaginis Filii sui, ut sit ipse primogenitus in multis fratribus. Quos autem praedestinavit, hos & vocavit, & quos vocavit, hos & justificavit, quos autem justificavit, hos & glorificavit. Nam, ultro caecus sit oportet, qui non agnoscat, ex mente Apostoli, justificationem esse aliquid medium inter vocationem & glorificationem.
pass_a_gloss: But especially here Paul's place in Romans 8:29-30 is greatly to be observed. Where the Apostle, weaving the series and chain of graces and benefits that flow from God's eternal love toward the elect, and recounting each in its order, expressly puts calling before justification as something that precedes it. For, he says, those whom he foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers. And those whom he predestined he also called, and those whom he called he also justified, and those whom he justified he also glorified. For one must be willfully blind who does not acknowledge that in the Apostle's mind justification is something intermediate between calling and glorification.
pass_b_english: Rom 8:30 orders calling before justification in the golden chain.
Justification sits between calling and glorification—not before faith's call.
